Ballia.x: Ballia is in Uttar Pradesh province of India. Ballia is an ancient city. Many great saints and sages of India had their ashrams in Ballia, including 'Valmiki', 'Bhrigu', 'Durvasa', 'Parashara muni' and 'Jamadagni.' Ballia was a part of the Kosala Kingdom in ancient times.

sights.d: Dadri Mela is the second largest cattle fair of India. The fair starts on the full moon of the month of Kartik (October–November) with a holy dip in the Ganges River.

Bangalore.x: Bangalore, officially called Bengaluru, is the largest city in southern India and the capital of the state of Karnataka. A cosmopolitan city, Bangalore was developed around what was once a mud fort of a feudal lord. The city has a population of nearly 13 million (2025), making it India's fourth-largest city.

Bir.x: Bir is a town in the eastern end of the Kangra Valley in Himachal Pradesh with a friendly, relaxed Indian population and a large Tibetan (Khampa) community. It is home to several educational institutions, monasteries, and nonprofit organizations (NGOs). It is becoming a popular off-the-beaten-path destination for meditation courses, volunteering, and ecotourism.

Byndoor.x: Byndoor is the northernmost taluka of Udupi district, spanning from the coast to the foothills of the western ghats. The Kollur Mookambika temple is located around 28 km from the town of Byndoor.

sights.d: Reached only by trekking to the deep jungle. The name "Arishna" refers to the orange-yellow colour created by sunrays falling on the water droplets around the waterfall.

Chittorgarh.x: Chittorgarh, also spelled Chittaurgarh, is in the southern part of Rajasthan, lies on the Berach River, a tributary of the Banas, and is the administrative headquarters of Chittorgharh District. It is 112 km from Udaipur and 182 km from Ajmer. The city served as a capital to the Sisodia clans of Rajputs of Mewar for a long time.

Kalaburagi.x: Kalaburagi, previously known as Gulbarga, is a city in Northern Karnataka and the head quarters of the Kalaburagi District. Gulburga literally means "city of gardens" while Kaliburagi means "rocky land." It was once the capital of the Bahmani Sultanate and an important Sufi centre.

Kannur.x: Kannur, formerly Cannanore, is a seaside city on the northern side of Kerala (Keralam), India. The Aralam Wildlife Sanctuary on the Western Ghats is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Kannur (old name Cannanore) is known as Land of Looms and Lore because of the importance of the fabric industry and the concentration of Theyyam temple dance festivals.

Mumbai.x: Mumbai, formerly known as Bombay, is the largest city in western India and the capital of the state of Maharashtra. The island was in turn joined with the neighbouring island of Salsette to form "Greater Bombay".
